flashcards.description: Flashcards are key to mastering fact-dense UPSC questions. Click on any card below to flip it and reveal the answer.

items.question: How did archaeologists prove the right-to-left writing direction of the script?
items.answer: By observing the cramping/compression of signs on the left margins of seals, showing the scribe ran out of space.

items.question: What is the estimated number of distinct signs in the logo-syllabic script?
items.answer: Between 375 and 400 signs, indicating it is not alphabetical but logo-syllabic.

items.question: Name the scholars associated with the Proto-Dravidian linguistic hypothesis.
Where was the 10-symbol public signboard discovered?
items.answer: Near the northern gateway of the Citadel at Dholavira, Gujarat.

items.question: What is the non-linguistic symbol hypothesis proposed by Farmer, Sproat, and Witzel?
items.answer: The theory that the script did not encode a spoken language but was a non-linguistic system of heraldic or ritual symbols.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the writing direction, physical inscriptions, and linguistic models of the Harappan Civilisation.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
विशेषताएं

  • लोगो-सिलेबिक प्रणाली
  • लगभग 400-500 चिन्ह
  • दिशा: दाएं से बाएं

भाषाई सिद्धांत

  • द्रविड़ परिकल्पना (अस्को परपोला)
  • इंडो-आर्यन/संस्कृत परिकल्पना
  • आदि-मुंडा संबंध
  • लिपि की संरचना
    • बौस्ट्रोफेडन: वैकल्पिक पंक्तियाँ दाएं-से-बाएं और बाएं-से-दाएं लिखी जाती थीं।
    • कोई लंबे शिलालेख नहीं; सामान्य लंबाई 5-10 अक्षर है।
    • चिन्ह सूची: मछली के चिन्ह सबसे आम हैं।
विशेषताविवरण
माध्यमसेलखड़ी की मुहरें, ताम्रपट्टिका, मिट्टी के बर्तन
पढ़ने की स्थितिकोई द्विभाषी 'रोज़ेटा स्टोन' नहीं मिला

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the writing direction of the Harappan script:
1. Scribes wrote from right to left, as evidenced by the compression of symbols on the left margin of seals.
2. In longer inscriptions, they utilized the Boustrophedon system, where lines alternate in direction.
3. The writing direction of Boustrophedon is unique to the Harappan civilisation and is not found in any other ancient civilisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Boustrophedon writing is not unique to the Harappans; it is also found in early ancient Greek and Sabaean inscriptions.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the nature of the Harappan script, consider the following statements:
1. It is a purely alphabetical script containing around 40 distinct characters.
2. The script is logo-syllabic, with each sign representing a word or a syllable.
3. The total number of identified distinct signs ranges between 375 and 400.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the script is logo-syllabic (375-400 signs), not alphabetical (which would require fewer than 40 characters).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dholavira Signboard finding:
1. It features ten large pictographic signs carved out of white gypsum crystalline paste.
2. The signs were mounted on a wooden frame and placed over the northern gateway of the Citadel.
3. It remains undeciphered, consistent with all other inscriptions discovered in the Indus valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the gypsum paste signs, gateway location, and undeciphered status of the Dholavira signboard.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the physical distribution of Harappan inscriptions, consider the following statements:
1. Script symbols are found engraved on square steatite seals, copper tablets, and clay pottery graffiti.
2. Writing was reserved exclusively for administrative seals and is completely absent on domestic household pottery.
3. Small copper tablets feature signs on one side and animal figures on the other, likely serving as trade tokens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: writing is frequently found as graffiti on domestic potsherds, indicating widespread domestic use or ownership markings.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dravidian hypothesis of the Harappan language:
1. Iravatham Mahadevan and Asko Parpola are the primary scholars who argued that the Harappan language belongs to the Proto-Dravidian family.
2. The 'fish' symbol is read as *min*, which represents both 'fish' and 'star' in Dravidian languages, denoting astral deities on seals.
3. This hypothesis has been completely accepted by all linguists, resolving the decipherment debate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the hypothesis remains a subject of intense academic debate and has not been universally accepted.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Indo-Aryan hypothesis of the Harappan language, consider the following statements:
1. Scholar S.R. Rao proposed that the Harappan script represents a precursor to the Sanskrit language.
2. Under this model, the script is read as an alphabetical system carrying Vedic phonetic sounds.
3. S.R. Rao's decipherment has been universally accepted by the Archaeological Survey of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: S.R. Rao's reading has been widely rejected by mainstream linguists who point out arbitrary sign values and lack of grammatical structure in his translations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the non-linguistic symbol hypothesis of the Indus script:
1. Steve Farmer, Richard Sproat, and Michael Witzel argued that the script did not encode a spoken language.
2. They point out the extreme brevity of inscriptions, with the average text containing only 4 to 5 signs.
3. They argue that the symbols served as heraldic coats-of-arms, clan emblems, or religious icons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and define the core arguments of the Farmer-Sproat-Witzel non-linguistic hypothesis.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the decipherment challenges of the Harappan script, consider the following statements:
1. Decipherment is blocked because no bilingual inscription containing a known language has been discovered.
2. The script lacks long texts; the longest known single inscription contains only 26 signs.
3. Modern computer analysis has proven that the script has no statistical similarity to any human language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: computer entropy analysis by Rajesh Rao and others showed the script's sign order behaves similarly to spoken human languages, contradicting the claim of no statistical similarity.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the symbol typology of the Harappan script:
1. The most frequently occurring sign is the 'fish' symbol, which has several variants with modifying strokes.
2. Jar or U-shaped symbols are also highly common, often appearing at the end of inscriptions.
3. The script completely lacks representations of human figures, focusing exclusively on geometric lines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: signs depicting human figures carrying bows, holding sticks, or sitting in yogic postures are present in the script corpus.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the writing instruments used by Harappan scribes, consider the following statements:
1. Small copper styluses and bone sticks were used to carve characters into wet clay and wax molds.
2. Large gypsum letters at Dholavira were cast in clay molds before being mounted on the wooden gate.
3. Paper-like birch bark sheets imported from the Himalayas were used for administrative letters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Dholavira gypsum signs were carved directly from stone or built using gypsum paste, not cast in clay molds. Statement 3 is incorrect: there is no archaeological evidence of birch bark sheets being used for writing in the IVC.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relation between Harappan script and punch-marked coins:
1. Several symbols on Maurya punch-marked coins resemble signs from the Harappan script.
2. This resemblance has been interpreted by some scholars as evidence of cultural and script continuity in India.
3. The Harappan script was directly used to denote coin values during the Mature Harappan phase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: coins did not exist in the Bronze Age Harappan economy; trade was carried out through barter and regulated weights, not coins.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Munda/Austroasiatic theory of the Harappan language, consider the following statements:
1. Some linguists suggest that the language belonged to the Austroasiatic or Munda language family.
2. This theory is supported by the presence of Munda loanwords in the early Rigveda, suggesting contacts in Northwest India.
3. This theory has successfully deciphered the script's animal symbols as Munda clan totems.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Munda theory has not deciphered the script; it remains an unproven hypothesis.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Boustrophedon writing style:
1. The term originates from Greek, meaning 'ox-turning', referring to the path of an ox plowing a field.
2. The scribe starts on the right, writes to the left, then continues on the next line writing left to right.
3. This style is also observed in early Sabaean (Yemeni) and Etruscan inscriptions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and define the origin, path, and other historical occurrences of the Boustrophedon style.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the sign compression on Harappan seals, consider the following statements:
1. Signs are often crowded and cramped on the left margin of the seal.
2. This cramping proves that the writing started on the right and moved leftwards.
3. The seal carving was done in reverse (mirror image) so that the clay impression would read correctly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the sign cramping, right-to-left direction, and mirror-image carving of seals.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the undeciphered status of the Harappan script:
1. Because it is undeciphered, we lack direct knowledge of Harappan religious mythology, names of rulers, or legal treaties.
2. All our knowledge of Harappan socio-political organization is derived solely from material remains and archaeology.
3. Deciphering the script would immediately clarify the relation between Harappan culture and later historical Indian traditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and describe the historical and archaeological consequences of the undeciphered script.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Dholavira Signboard gypsum letters, consider the following statements:
1. Each symbol is approximately 37 cm high and 25 to 27 cm wide.
2. The board was placed above a gate to declare the name of the ruling king.
3. The wood backing of the signboard decayed over time, leaving the gypsum inlays in the soil.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the exact text is undeciphered, and there is no evidence that it declared the name of a king, as monarchy is not proven.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding script signs on pottery:
1. Signs written as post-firing graffiti on domestic pots were likely ownership or quantity marks.
2. Pre-firing stamps on pottery indicate standardized industrial workshop markings.
3. Writing on pottery is only found in elite Citadel quarters and is absent in Lower Towns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: pottery graffiti containing script signs is widely found throughout the Lower Town quarters of commoners.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the average length of Harappan texts, consider the following statements:
1. The average inscription length is extremely short, containing only about 5 signs.
2. The shortest inscriptions consist of a single symbol.
3. The brevity of texts suggests they were names, titles, or trade quantities rather than narrative literature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the brevity of inscriptions and its implications for text interpretation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the fish symbol in the Harappan script:
1. The fish symbol is often modified with diacritical marks or strokes.
2. In Dravidian, the word for fish (*min*) is a homophone for star (*min*), suggesting astronomical associations.
3. The fish symbol is completely absent on copper tablets, appearing only on steatite seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the fish sign is present on all classes of inscriptions, including copper tablets and pottery graffiti.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the script signs on ivory rods, consider the following statements:
1. Engraved ivory sticks or rods have been excavated from Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.
2. These rods carry script signs and were likely used as measuring scales or gaming dice.
3. Ivory writing confirms the elite consumption of script-associated luxury goods.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, detailing the ivory rod findings, usage, and social status associations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the logo-syllabic nature of writing:
1. A logo-syllabic script uses signs that represent both whole words (logograms) and phonetic syllables.
2. Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs and Mesopotamian cuneiform are examples of logo-syllabic scripts.
3. The number of signs in a logo-syllabic script is typically in the hundreds, matching the Harappan sign count.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and define the structural features of a logo-syllabic script.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to S.R. Rao's decipherment methodology, consider the following statements:
1. S.R. Rao claimed that the late Harappan script evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.
2. He assigned West Semitic phonetic values to Harappan signs to read them as Sanskrit words.
3. S.R. Rao's Sanskrit readings have been widely accepted by international Semitic linguists.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Rao's readings are rejected for arbitrary phonetic assignments and forcing Indo-Aryan values on logo-syllabic signs.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the fish symbol variants:
1. Scribes added 'fins' or 'roofs' over the basic fish sign to create compound logograms.
2. Asko Parpola interpreted these variants as names of planets and deities (e.g., *Pasu-min* for Halley's Comet).
3. The variants show that the script had a highly systematic grammar of sign modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing sign modification, Parpola's planet readings, and systematic sign grammar.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the writing on clay sealings, consider the following statements:
1. Sealings are clay tags stamped with seals, used to secure cargo bags of grain and cotton.
2. The backs of sealings often show impressions of woven reeds, mats, or leather cords.
3. Sealings prove that the script played a central role in validating trade ownership and customs clearance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing clay sealings, reed back-impressions, and trade validation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the script sign count:
1. If a script has under 50 signs, it is alphabetical; if in the hundreds, it is logo-syllabic; if in the thousands, it is logo-graphic.
2. The Harappan sign count of ~400 proves it represents a logo-syllabic system.
3. The sign count indicates that literacy required memorizing hundreds of characters, likely restricting writing to professional scribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, outlining script typology, sign counts, and professional scribe status.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Boustrophedon direction indicator, consider the following statements:
1. The direction of writing alternates from right-to-left in line 1, then left-to-right in line 2.
2. This system prevented the scribe from having to return the stylus to the opposite margin, speeding up writing.
3. The Boustrophedon style is only found in Indian languages and is absent in Europe.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Boustrophedon is a Greek term and was widely used in early Greek and Anatolian inscriptions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the steatite seals:
1. Seals were carved in negative (reverse) relief so that the stamped clay impressions would appear in positive relief.
2. The text on the seals reads correctly (from right-to-left) when viewed on the clay sealing itself.
3. Scribes carved both the animal figures and the text signs with extreme precision using chert burins.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing reverse carving, correct reading on sealings, and chert tool precision.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the longest Harappan inscription, consider the following statements:
1. The longest single inscription contains 26 signs on a three-sided steatite baton.
2. No tablet, seal, or pottery has yielded a long text of over 50 signs.
3. The lack of long texts makes structural grammatical analysis of the language extremely difficult.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing the 26-sign baton, lack of long texts, and grammatical analysis blocks.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indus script variants over time:
1. The script remained highly static, showing little evolution over the 700 years of the mature phase.
2. Scribes in Punjab and Gujarat used identical sign lists, proving centralized standards.
3. The late Harappan phase shows a decline in seal quality and gradual disappearance of the script.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing script stability, identical regional signs, and late phase decline.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the Rigveda and Harappan language, consider the following statements:
1. The Rigveda contains several non-Indo-Aryan words identified as Proto-Dravidian loanwords.
2. This linguistic layering suggests that Rigvedic speakers encountered Dravidian-like speakers in the Indus basin.
3. The Rigveda directly describes the Boustrophedon writing style of the Meluhhans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Rigveda is an oral text that does not describe the Harappan script or writing direction.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the fish symbol reading *min*:
1. *Min* is the Proto-Dravidian word for 'fish'.
2. The homophone *min* also means 'star' or 'shining' in Dravidian languages.
3. This homophonic reading is used to interpret fish symbols on seals as names of stars or astral deities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and define the core linguistic rebus puzzle of the Dravidian reading.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the writing on pottery jars, consider the following statements:
1. Post-firing graffiti was scratched using sharp stone burins.
2. Jars at Harappa show sequence numbers, likely indicating shipment counts.
3. Writing on pots was done using ink made from charcoal and animal fat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: there is no archaeological evidence of charcoal-fat ink being used on pots; writing was incised or scratched, not painted with ink.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the signboards at Dholavira:
1. The wooden board was mounted over the gateway to the Citadel Castle.
2. The gypsum characters are made of pure plaster of Paris.
3. It represents a public declaration of civic authority and administrative literacy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: characters were made of natural crystalline gypsum paste, which is chemically hydrous calcium sulfate, not modern processed plaster of Paris.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to S.R. Rao's alphabetical decipherment, consider the following statements:
1. He read the signs from left to right, reversing the standard direction.
2. He translated the text as Vedic Sanskrit names like *Aka*, *Rama*, and *Sada*.
3. His translations have been dismissed as arbitrary and lacking phonetic consistency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. S.R. Rao read the signs from right-to-left but forced Semitic values to extract Sanskrit words. His readings are widely dismissed.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the sign cramping on the left:
1. Scribes underestimated seal dimensions, starting on the right and squeezing letters on the left.
2. This cramping proves that the seals were meant to be read directly, not stamped.
3. Cramping is only observed on copper tablets and is absent on steatite seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: cramping on the seal was mirrored, and it proved that the stamped clay tags (read right-to-left) were the primary media. Statement 3 is incorrect: cramping is common on steatite seals.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the writing on ivory sticks, consider the following statements:
1. Ivory sticks feature short sign inscriptions alongside geometric grid marks.
2. They were likely used as administrative counters, luxury dice, or weavers' tools.
3. Ivory rods were exported to Egypt, where they were placed in Pharaohs' tombs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: there is no evidence of Harappan ivory rods being exported to Egyptian royal tombs.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the undeciphered script's impact on Indian history:
1. It prevents us from verifying if the Rigveda was written by Harappan citizens.
2. It leaves the transition between the Indus valley and Gangetic civilisations highly debated.
3. Deciphering the script would confirm the linguistic roots of early Indian urbanism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the key historical debates linked to the undeciphered script.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the sign modification system, consider the following statements:
1. Scribes added short strokes, dots, or diagonal lines to primary signs to modify their values.
2. Modified signs behave like vowel signs in historical Indian scripts (e.g. *matras*).
3. This systematic modification suggests a highly structured phonology and script conventions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct and define the sign modification system and its phonetic implications.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the fish symbol variants read as planets:
1. Asko Parpola argued that the fish symbol (*min*) represented stars or planets.
2. The modified fish with a roof was read as *Velli-min* (Venus/White Star).
3. S.R. Rao read the fish symbol as a letter value *ma* based on phonetic Semitic comparisons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, detailing Parpola's planetary readings and Rao's alphabetical comparisons.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the writing on storage jars, consider the following statements:
1. Large black-slipped storage jars feature deeply incised script signs.
2. These jars were used for exporting goods to Oman and the Persian Gulf.
3. The incised signs likely indicated the exporter's seal, contents, or weights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the export storage jars, Omani findings, and sign functions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographical distribution of Harappan writing:
1. Script symbols are discovered as far as Shortughai in Badakhshan, Afghanistan.
2. Inscribed pottery fragments have also been recovered from Ras al-Jinz in Oman, proving maritime trade links.
3. No Harappan script has ever been found outside the geographical borders of modern India and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Harappan inscriptions have been found in Afghanistan (Shortughai), Oman (Ras al-Jinz), and Mesopotamia (Ur, Kish).

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the relationship between the Indus script and administrative control, consider the following statements:
1. The standardization of sign shapes across distant cities indicates central administrative oversight.
2. The disappearance of writing coincides precisely with the collapse of mature urban municipal bodies.
3. Writing was utilized to record detailed treaties between the Citadel elites and rural chieftains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: because the script is undeciphered, we have no evidence of written treaties or political documents.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the rebus writing technique:
1. Rebus writing uses pictographic representations of concrete objects to denote homophones with abstract meanings.
2. This technique was also a key step in the development of ancient Egyptian and Sumerian scripts.
3. Rebus writing has been completely ruled out by all scholars analyzing the Harappan script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: rebus writing is the primary method used by scholars like Asko Parpola to propose readings for the script.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the language family of the Harappan Civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. The Austroasiatic (Munda) family is connected to the Indus Valley through prehistoric substrate influences.
2. The Indo-Aryan Sanskrit model requires reading the signs alphabetically from left to right.
3. The Proto-Dravidian hypothesis remains the most archaeologically and geographically plausible theory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the key arguments and structures of the Munda, Indo-Aryan, and Dravidian linguistic models.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dholavira Signboard's physical construction:
1. Each of the ten symbols was carved from natural white gypsum paste.
2. The gypsum symbols were inlaid into a large wooden board that hung over the Citadel gate.
3. The letters were coated with gold leaf to make them shine under sunlight.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: there is no archaeological evidence of gold leaf coatings on the Dholavira signboard letters.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the script symbols representing numbers, consider the following statements:
1. Scribes represented numbers using simple vertical strokes or bars.
2. The number strokes are often grouped together to represent units and tens.
3. Number signs are frequently placed before U-shaped or jar-shaped symbols.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing number representation, grouping of strokes, and placement before jar symbols.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Boustrophedon writing layout:
1. It allowed the reader to read continuously without moving their eyes back to the start margin.
2. Scribes curved the shapes of the boundary signs to transition between lines.
3. It was exclusively reserved for public signboards and was never used on seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Boustrophedon is found on longer inscriptions on seals and potsherds, while the Dholavira signboard is a single line.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the decipherment attempts of John Marshall, consider the following statements:
1. John Marshall officially declared the script undeciphered during his excavations in the 1920s.
2. He suggested a tentative connection to early Dravidian language families.
3. Marshall argued that the script was imported directly from Egypt during the Old Kingdom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: John Marshall did not suggest the script was imported from Egypt; he recognized its indigenous origin.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the fish symbol reading in astronomic calendars:
1. Parpola interpreted the fish sign with a roof as Venus, associated with the Dravidian word for white.
2. Scribes placed the fish symbol adjacent to deity figures on seals to denote astral protection.
3. The fish symbol is completely absent on copper tablets found at Harappa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the fish symbol is present on various copper tablets from both Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the post-urban script usage (Late Harappan phase), consider the following statements:
1. Inscriptions became rare and signs simplified, losing their pictorial clarity.
2. The use of elaborate steatite seals with animal reliefs ceased entirely.
3. Graffiti on pottery survived as the last remnants of the writing system before its demise.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the simplification of signs, cessation of steatite seals, and survival of pottery graffiti in the Late Harappan phase.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the writing direction of the Harappan script:
1. Scribes primarily wrote from right to left, proven by the cramping of symbols on the left of seals.
2. In longer inscriptions, they wrote in Boustrophedon direction, alternating lines from right-to-left and left-to-right.
3. The Boustrophedon writing style is completely unique to India and is absent in European antiquities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Boustrophedon is a Greek term meaning 'ox-turning' and was used in early Greek and Sabaean inscriptions.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the logo-syllabic nature of the script, consider the following statements:
1. The script contains between 375 and 400 distinct signs, proving it is not alphabetical.
2. Each sign represents either a whole word (logogram) or a syllable sound.
3. The undeciphered status of the script leaves the spoken language of the IVC unknown.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, describing the logo-syllabic sign count, syllables, and language implications of the undeciphered script.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding S.R. Rao's Sanskrit decipherment:
1. He read the signs alphabetically by assigning Semitic phonetic values to them.
2. S.R. Rao's Sanskrit readings have been widely accepted by the Linguistic Society of India.
3. His translations read Vedic Sanskrit words like 'Rama', 'Aka', and 'Sada' on trade seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: S.R. Rao's decipherment has been rejected by most linguists due to arbitrary sign assignments and lack of grammatical coherence.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the Dravidian theory of the Harappan language, consider the following statements:
1. Linguist Asko Parpola argued that the language belongs to the Proto-Dravidian family.
2. Scribes used the rebus principle, reading the fish sign (*min*) as star/planet (*min*).
3. This theory has been universally proven and accepted as the final decipherment key.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Proto-Dravidian reading remains a strong hypothesis but is not universally accepted or proven.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dholavira Signboard:
1. It features ten large symbols made of white crystalline gypsum paste.
2. Scribes mounted the characters on a wooden board over the northern gate of the Citadel.
3. It represents a public notification of civic or administrative authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and define the material, location, and administrative significance of the Dholavira signboard.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the non-linguistic symbol theory of Farmer, Sproat, and Witzel, consider the following statements:
1. They argued that the Indus script did not encode a spoken language.
2. The extreme brevity of inscriptions (average of 5 signs) supports this theory.
3. They suggested the signs served as heraldic emblems, clan symbols, or ritual codes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, describing the key arguments and symbol explanations of the non-linguistic theory.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the physical writing media:
1. Steatite seals and clay pottery graffiti carry the largest volume of script signs.
2. Large copper plates and small copper tablets also feature script engravings.
3. Paper-like materials made of papyrus have been excavated from Mohenjo-daro houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: papyrus was used in ancient Egypt, and no such paper-like organic writing sheets have survived in the Indus Valley.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the sign modification system, consider the following statements:
1. Scribes added auxiliary strokes, dots, and lines to main signs to change their meaning.
2. The modification behaves similarly to the vowel markings (*matras*) in historical Indian scripts.
3. This systematic modification suggests a highly structured script convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct, outlining the sign modifiers, matra-like behavior, and structured script conventions.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the longest Indus text:
1. The longest single inscription contains 26 signs on a three-sided steatite baton.
2. No text has been recovered that exceeds 50 signs, suggesting a lack of long narrative literature.
3. The brevity of texts makes it difficult to verify grammar, syntax, or word order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct, detailing the 26-sign record, lack of narrative texts, and grammatical analysis blocks.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the fish symbol variants in Parpola's Dravidian readings, consider the following statements:
1. The modified fish with a roof was read as *Velli-min* (Venus/White Star).
2. The modified fish with a diagonal stroke was read as *Paci-min* (Green Star/Mercury).
3. These readings provide a coherent model of Harappan astronomical calendars.
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct and represent Parpola's reconstructed astronomic readings based on Dravidian homophones.

traps.title: यूपीएससी परीक्षा के सामान्य जाल
items: लिपि को वर्णमाला प्रणाली समझना; यह संभवतः लोगो-सिलेबिक (चिन्ह-ध्वनि) है।
भाषा को वैदिक संस्कृत मानना; दोनों को जोड़ने वाला कोई भाषाई प्रमाण नहीं है।
यह सोचना कि लिपि पढ़ ली गई है; एस.आर. राव जैसे विद्वानों के दावे अकादमिक रूप से असत्यापित हैं।
